correctness.rationale: Using E(y)^2/y²−1=Σ Ω_i(y^{q_i}−1)=(y−1)F(y), with F=ΣΩ_i (y^{q_i}−1)/(y−1), the drift sign is minus sign F for E,y>0. F(1+)=ΣΩ_i q_i=2q0. For q<0 or q>1, φ_q is strictly increasing on y>1 by derivative g_q'=q(1−q)y^{q−2}(y−1)<0 and g_q(1)=1. φ_1≡1; φ_0≡0. Hence F is nondecreasing and, whenever q0<0, strictly increasing. The mandatory positive q>=1 fluid makes F eventually positive (q=1 constant positive or q>1 divergent) while negative-q contributions tend to zero from below. This proves existence and uniqueness iff q0<0; at q0=0 F immediately positive. For no accelerating component all q>=1, F positive. Curvature cancels by normalization; no restriction Ωk sign beyond H>0 and normalization. Independent exact algebra and ΛCDM root z≈2.08876043244513 (Ωm=.3, ΩΛ=.7) confirm the illustrative case; finite example is not the theorem proof.
residual_risks: Requires H(z)>0 for all y>=1; arbitrary negative curvature without positive expanding branch would invalidate sign inference.
Excluded -1/3<w<0 gives 0<q<1 and decreasing φ, so uniqueness argument does not extend.

value.rationale: The existence and number of positive-redshift drift sign changes are natural global observables in standard constant equation-of-state cosmologies. Unlike mere root formulas or numerical plots, the theorem provides a sharp, all-mixture topological root count in terms of the local observable q0, even with curvature; the exponent separation explains exactly why it works. This is an independently useful structural lemma, albeit short and confined to a physically motivated but not universal fluid class.
residual_risks: No observational inference, varying-w, interacting, exotic fluid or mixed-sign density model.

final_claim: For expanding FLRW models with finitely many nonnegative-density noninteracting constant-w fluids having q=1+3w either q<0 or q>=1 (q=0 absorbed as curvature), at least one positive-density q>=1 fluid, and H(z)>0 on y=1+z>=1, the redshift drift has exactly one positive-z zero iff present deceleration q0<0; otherwise strictly negative, with curvature canceling from the root equation.
limitations: Requires positive density q>=1, excludes -1/3<w<0 and other cosmological generalizations.
Originality limited by near-covering FLRW literature.
